# GitHub Copilot Instructions

This repository is a simple fork/spoon-knife example project used to demonstrate GitHub forking and pull requests.

## Project Overview

This is a basic HTML/CSS website project that serves as a practice repository for learning about:
- Forking repositories
- Making pull requests
- Contributing to open source projects

## Code Style Guidelines

### HTML
- Use proper indentation (2 spaces)
- Include proper DOCTYPE declarations
- Use semantic HTML5 elements where appropriate
- Keep inline styles to a minimum; prefer external CSS

### CSS
- Use clear, descriptive selector names
- Maintain consistent spacing (a basic CSS reset with zero margins/padding is applied via the `*` selector)
- Keep styles organized and commented when necessary
- Use shorthand properties where appropriate

### Markdown
- Use proper heading hierarchy
- Keep lines reasonably short for readability
- Include links using descriptive text
- Use proper formatting for code blocks when needed

## General Guidelines

- Keep changes minimal and focused
- Maintain the existing simple structure
- Test any HTML/CSS changes in a browser
- Ensure all links and references work correctly
- Keep the playful, welcoming tone of the project

## Documentation

- Update README.md if adding new features or changing functionality
- Keep documentation clear and beginner-friendly
- Include examples where helpful

## Testing

- Manually test HTML pages in a browser
- Verify CSS changes don't break existing styling
- Check that all links work correctly
- Ensure the site remains accessible and simple

## Project Goals

Remember: This is an educational project meant to help people learn about GitHub collaboration. Keep changes simple, clear, and welcoming to newcomers.
